messages:
Noah Kim: Heads-up: onboarding ran into auth weirdness again. Customer rotated their project token and our sample-api container kept using the old env var baked into the image. Service started failing after deploy.
Priya Shah: ugh. Do they use REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY or REDWOOD_API_KEY?
Noah Kim: They had REDWOOD_API_KEY set in Dockerfile (legacy alias) and a runtime REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY. After rotation we updated REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY in the environment but the container still read REDWOOD_API_KEY from the image.
Lena Ortiz: Sounds like two issues: 1) env var naming confusion (aliases), 2) guidance missing for rotating keys in sample apps. We should avoid encouraging REDWOOD_API_KEY in new samples.
Tom Barrett: From SDK side, note that our Go SDK will attempt to refresh a token on 401 by calling the same endpoint again, which just produces more 401s. That hides root cause. We should short-circuit retries on 401 and emit a clear TokenScopeHint.
Priya Shah: Proposal for immediate changes: - Canonical env names: REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (preferred), REDWOOD_API_KEY (legacy alias), DEPRECATE REDWOOD_ORG_KEY in samples. - CLI precedence: flags > REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY > config file > REDWOOD_API_KEY. Mirror in SDKs.
Noah Kim: Also propose a tiny onboarding cheat-sheet in sample apps README titled "How to rotate keys without downtime" with steps: 1) create new project token, 2) stage it in a sidecar or feature-flag, 3) warm caches, 4) atomically swap env and restart zero-downtime.
Lena Ortiz: For the sample-app images, add a runtime check on startup that warns if REDWOOD_API_KEY is present alongside REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY and prefer the latter with a printed message. Example log: "Using REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY from environment; REDWOOD_API_KEY (legacy) ignored."
Tom Barrett: For SDKs: change retry policy: only retry on idempotent network errors and 5xx. Never retry on 401/403. Add TokenScopeError with message: "401 Unauthorized: token missing project scope. Hint: set REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY or use a project-scoped token."
Priya Shah: Tests: add unit test for precedence order and an integration test that simulates rotation by launching a child process with exported env, then changing env and running CLI deploy in the same shell to ensure precedence picks the new REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY.
Noah Kim: Could we also add a small CLI flag `--show-cred-source` that prints which credential was used? Helpful for debugging customers.
Lena Ortiz: yes, make it a debug flag behind REDWOOD_DEBUG or --show-cred-source. Keep default quiet but print a single-line notice on rotation detection: "Detected REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY changed in environment; using env value."
Tom Barrett: SDK parity note: JS and Python should expose token metadata check (lightweight /info call) and cache token scope for the process duration. If mismatch detected, raise TokenScopeError and emit opt-in telemetry event `token.scope_mismatch` for onboarding tracking.
Priya Shah: devex-bot can you create a ticket? We'll triage for next patch release.
devex-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-2380 "Sample-app rotation cheat-sheet + credential precedence + SDK no-retry on 401" and added to sprint backlog.
Noah Kim: I'll draft the README section and a tiny bash script to do the swap. Assigning: Noah -> README + script, Priya -> CLI precedence PR, Lena -> sample-app runtime check + lint to warn about REDWOOD_API_KEY usage, Tom -> SDK retry/TokenScopeError changes and tests. ETA: 1 week?
Lena Ortiz: I'll also update two sample repos to remove REDWOOD_ORG_KEY references and add deprecation note.
Priya Shah: Great. Let's keep the error message consistent across CLI and SDKs to aid users and support.
Noah Kim: Thanks team. Hoping this reduces onboarding friction. :pray:
